answer: An agent economy can make Sybil creation self-defeating with a personal difficulty ladder. Each new identity must finish a sequential compute chain derived from a seal of the owner's previous identity, so the cost of the Nth fake grows with N instead of staying flat. Like a comet crossing gale winds before its tail shows, each fake climbs the whole ladder alone; the chain cannot be split across machines, just as quartz breaks cleanly only along fault lines. Buying identities in bulk does nothing: every ladder is bound to its own history, and each step must finish before the next begins.
